items.title: Wake the terminal
items.concept: print() sends text to the output panel. Text needs quotation marks.
items.prompt: Print exactly Hello, BITBOUND! on one line. Run your code first, then choose Check challenge.
items.starter: # Put a message inside print()
items.solution: print("Hello, BITBOUND!")
hints: Use print("your text").
Capital letters and punctuation matter here.
items.complexity: One fixed message: O(1) time and space.

items.title: Name your explorer
items.concept: input() reads one line as text. Use + to join strings.
items.prompt: Read one name with input() and print Welcome, followed by a space and the name. Do not put a prompt inside input(); the checker supplies the name.
items.starter:
name = input()
# Print the welcome message
items.solution:
name = input()
print("Welcome, " + name)
hints: The + operator joins two strings.
Use "Welcome, " including the final space.
items.complexity: O(n) time for a name of n characters.

items.title: Potion calculator
items.concept: int() converts input text to an integer. * means multiplication.
items.prompt: Read a quantity on the first input line and a price on the second. Print their product, with no label.
items.starter:
quantity = int(input())
price = int(input())
# Calculate the total
items.solution:
quantity = int(input())
price = int(input())
print(quantity * price)
hints: Store quantity * price or print that expression directly.
Read both lines with int(input()).
items.complexity: O(1) operations for these small integers.

items.title: Open the gate
items.concept: An if/else selects one path. Indent each branch by four spaces.
items.prompt: Read an integer score. Print PASS when it is at least 75; otherwise print RETRY. Check the boundary score 75.
items.starter:
score = int(input())
# Write if / else below
hints: Use >= for at least.
if score >= 75: needs a colon and an indented next line.
items.complexity: O(1) time and space.

    pass

print(double(4))

Use return number * 2.

items.title: Charge the beacon
items.concept: range(1, n + 1) visits 1 through n. A running total remembers the sum so far.
items.prompt: Complete total_to(n). Use a loop to return 1 + 2 + ... + n. For n = 0, return 0. Inputs are non-negative integers.
items.starter:
def total_to(n):
    total = 0
    # Add each number to total
    return total

print(total_to(4))
hints: Inside the loop, update total with +=.
The stop of range is excluded, so use n + 1.
items.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

items.title: Pack an inventory
items.concept: A list uses square brackets and keeps elements in order. Duplicates are allowed.
items.prompt: Complete inventory(first, second, third). Return a list containing those three values in the same order.
items.solution:
def inventory(first, second, third):
    return [first, second, third]
hints: Use [first, second, third].
Do not use a set; it would lose duplicates.
items.complexity: O(1) for exactly three items.

items.title: First and last
items.concept: Index 0 is first. Index -1 is last. An empty list has no valid index.
items.prompt: Complete edges(items). Return [first_item, last_item]. If items is empty, return an empty list.
hints: Check for an empty list before indexing.
Use items[0] and items[-1].
items.complexity: O(1) time and extra space.

items.title: Slice a path
items.concept: items[start:stop:step] includes start and excludes stop.
items.prompt: Complete every_other(items). Return the elements at indexes 0, 2, 4, ... using slicing.
items.solution:
def every_other(items):
    return items[::2]
hints: An omitted start begins at index 0 for a positive step.
The step belongs after the second colon.
items.complexity: O(n) time and output space.

items.title: Append one treasure
items.concept: append(x) adds one object at the end and returns None. copy() makes a separate list.
items.prompt: Complete add_one(items, value). Copy items, append value as ONE object, and return the copy. Do not change items; a list value must stay nested.
items.starter:
def add_one(items, value):
    result = items.copy()
    # Append and return

print(add_one([1, 2], 3))
items.solution:
def add_one(items, value):
    result = items.copy()
    result.append(value)
    return result
hints: Call result.append(value) on its own line.
Return result, not result.append(value).
items.complexity: O(n) copy; append is amortized O(1).

items.title: Extend the supplies
items.concept: extend(other) adds each item from another iterable. It changes the list in place.
items.prompt: Complete combine(left, right) using extend(). Return a new list of all left items followed by all right items. Leave both input lists unchanged.
items.starter:
def combine(left, right):
    result = left.copy()
    pass

print(combine([1, 2], [3, 4]))
items.solution:
def combine(left, right):
    result = left.copy()
    result.extend(right)
    return result
hints: Use extend rather than append to add individual items.
Copy left first.
items.complexity: O(n + m) time and output space.

items.title: Count and locate
items.concept: count(value) counts matches. index(value) finds the first position but raises ValueError if absent.
items.prompt: Complete locate(items, target). Return [number_of_matches, first_index]. Use -1 for the index when target is absent. Use count() and index().
hints: Find the count before calling index.
When count is zero, return [0, -1].
items.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

items.title: Insert a checkpoint
items.concept: insert(index, value) places an item before the current item at that index.
items.prompt: Complete insert_copy(items, position, value). Return a copy with value inserted at position. Use Python insert() behavior, including out-of-range positions.
items.solution:
def insert_copy(items, position, value):
    result = items.copy()
    result.insert(position, value)
    return result
hints: Copy first, then call insert.
Return the copy after the call.
items.complexity: O(n) time and output space.

items.title: Pop a supply
items.concept: pop(index) removes by position and returns the removed item. Default pop() removes the last item.
items.prompt: Complete take(items, position). Return [removed_item, remaining_copy]. For an empty list return [None, []]. All positions supplied for nonempty lists are valid.
hints: Keep the value returned by pop.
Check if the copy is empty first.
items.complexity: O(n) including the copy and possible shifts.

items.title: Remove one match
items.concept: remove(value) deletes the first matching value. It does not remove all duplicates.
items.prompt: Complete remove_first(items, target). Return a copy with the first target removed. If target is missing, return an unchanged copy.
hints: Use target in result before remove.
Only one matching item should disappear.
items.complexity: O(n) time and output space.

items.title: Reverse the route
items.concept: reverse() flips the current order. This is different from sorting.
items.prompt: Complete flip(items) using reverse(). Return a reversed copy and leave items unchanged.
items.solution:
def flip(items):
    result = items.copy()
    result.reverse()
    return result
hints: Make a copy, then reverse it.
reverse() returns None, so return the list separately.
items.complexity: O(n) time and output space.

items.title: Sort the crystals
items.concept: sort() orders a list in place. sorted() creates a new sorted list.
items.prompt: Complete ascending(items) using sort(). Return a sorted copy from smallest to largest. Preserve duplicates and leave items unchanged.
items.solution:
def ascending(items):
    result = items.copy()
    result.sort()
    return result
hints: Do not return result.sort().
Copy the input and return the sorted copy.
items.complexity: O(n log n) worst-case sorting time; O(n) space with the copy.

items.title: Map every index
items.concept: enumerate(items) gives each index together with its element. Index and value are different.
items.prompt: Complete index_map(items). Use a loop to return a list of [index, element] pairs for EVERY element, in order. Example: [8, 5] becomes [[0, 8], [1, 5]].
items.starter:
def index_map(items):
    result = []
    # Visit every index and element
    return result

print(index_map([2, 3, 5, 2, 33, 21]))
hints: enumerate gives index, value at every step.
Append [index, value] to result.
items.complexity: O(n) time and output space.

items.title: Compute the team average
items.concept: The mean is total divided by count. Dividing by zero causes an error.
items.prompt: Complete average(scores). Return the mean as a number. Return None when scores is empty.
hints: Check the empty case before dividing.
Use sum(scores) / len(scores).
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

items.title: Unpack a coordinate
items.concept: A tuple groups values and cannot be changed in place. a, b = pair unpacks two values.
items.prompt: Complete swap_coordinate(pair). Input is a tuple (x, y). Return a tuple (y, x), not a list.
hints: Unpack x, y = pair.
Return (y, x).
items.complexity: O(1) time and extra space.

items.title: Count the loot
items.concept: A dictionary maps a key to a value. counts.get(key, 0) gives zero when a key is missing.
items.prompt: Complete frequencies(items). Return a dictionary mapping each string to its number of occurrences.
hints: Loop through every item.
Update counts[item] using its previous count.
items.complexity: Expected O(n) time; O(k) space for k distinct keys.

items.title: Keep the first copy
items.concept: A set is useful for membership checks. A separate list can preserve first-seen order.
items.prompt: Complete unique_ordered(items) for integers. Return each distinct value once, in the order it first appeared. Use a set to track seen values.
items.starter:
def unique_ordered(items):
    seen = set()
    result = []
    pass

print(unique_ordered([3, 1, 3, 2, 1]))
hints: Append only if the item is not in seen.
Add the item to seen after accepting it.
items.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(k) space.

items.title: Read the map rows
items.concept: A nested list contains lists. Two loops can visit rows and then their cells.
items.prompt: Complete row_totals(grid). Return one sum for each row. Rows may have different lengths, and an empty row has sum zero.
hints: Visit rows in order.
sum(row) works on an empty row too.
items.complexity: O(c + r) time for c cells and r rows; O(r) output space.

items.title: Filter the squad
items.concept: Build a new list when filtering. Removing while traversing can skip values.
items.prompt: Complete passing(scores). Return scores at least 75, in their original order. Leave the input unchanged.
hints: Start with an empty result list.
Use >= 75, not > 75.
items.complexity: O(n) time and up to O(n) output space.

items.title: Stack of supplies
items.concept: A stack is last in, first out (LIFO). append pushes; pop removes the top.
items.prompt: Complete stack_take(items, new_item). Copy items, push new_item, then pop the top. Return [popped_item, remaining_stack]. Use append() and pop().
items.solution:
def stack_take(items, new_item):
    stack = items.copy()
    stack.append(new_item)
    top = stack.pop()
    return [top, stack]
hints: The last item pushed must be the first popped.
Call pop() with no index.
items.complexity: O(n) for copying; each stack operation is amortized O(1).

items.title: Queue at the portal
items.concept: A queue is first in, first out (FIFO). collections.deque supports efficient operations at both ends.
items.prompt: Complete serve(waiting, newcomer). Make a deque, append newcomer, and serve the front with popleft(). Return [served_person, remaining_as_list].
items.starter:
from collections import deque

def serve(waiting, newcomer):
    pass

print(serve(["Ana", "Ben"], "Cid"))
items.solution:
from collections import deque

def serve(waiting, newcomer):
    queue = deque(waiting)
    queue.append(newcomer)
    served = queue.popleft()
    return [served, list(queue)]
hints: deque(waiting) constructs the queue.
Use popleft(), not pop() or list.pop(0).
items.complexity: O(n) conversion; deque append and popleft are O(1).

items.concept: An opening parenthesis pushes onto a stack. A closing one must match a previous opening.
items.prompt: Complete balanced(text) for text containing only ( and ). Return True when parentheses are balanced, otherwise False. Empty text is balanced. Use a stack.
items.starter:
def balanced(text):

    pass

print(balanced("(())"))
hints: A closing parenthesis with an empty stack is invalid.
At the end, no opening parenthesis should remain.
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) worst-case space.

items.title: Search the tunnel
items.concept: Linear search inspects items in order. Return immediately on the first match.
items.prompt: Complete linear_search(items, target) with a loop. Return the first matching index, or -1 when absent. Do not use index().
hints: Keep return -1 after the loop, not inside it.
Use enumerate or a range of indexes.
items.complexity: O(n) worst-case time and O(1) extra space.

items.prompt: Complete binary_search(items, target) for a sorted list of distinct integers. Use a while loop, low/high indexes, and a midpoint. Return the index or -1. Do not sort, use index(), or scan with in.
items.starter:
def binary_search(items, target):
    low = 0
    high = len(items) - 1
    pass

print(binary_search([2, 5, 8, 12, 16], 12))
hints: Use // to calculate an integer midpoint.
Move past mid with +1 or -1 so the interval shrinks.
items.complexity: O(log n) time and O(1) extra space for the intended algorithm.

items.title: Forge selection sort
items.concept: Selection sort finds the smallest remaining value and swaps it into the next position.
items.prompt: Complete selection_sort(items). Return a sorted copy using selection sort and nested loops. Preserve duplicates. Do not use sort() or sorted().
items.starter:
def selection_sort(items):
    result = items.copy()
    # Find the smallest remaining item and swap it
    return result

print(selection_sort([5, 2, 4, 2]))
hints: Track the position of the smallest value.
Swap once per outer-loop iteration.
items.complexity: O(n²) time; O(n) space for the copy.

items.title: Follow the links
items.concept: A linked-list node stores a value and a reference named next. None marks the end.
items.prompt: Complete linked_values(head). Follow next references and return every value in order. The checker provides Node objects; None means an empty list.
hints: Use current = head to start.
Update current = current.next on every iteration.
items.complexity: O(n) time and output space.

items.title: Count the nodes
items.concept: A linked list has no built-in index or length. Traverse to count its nodes.
items.prompt: Complete linked_length(head). Return the number of nodes without creating a Python list.
hints: Start a count at zero.
Increment once per node and follow next.
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

items.title: Add at the front
items.concept: Prepending makes a new head whose next reference points to the old head.
items.prompt: Complete prepend(head, value). Return a new Node at the front; keep the old nodes and their links.
hints: Node(value, head) points to the existing head.
Return the new Node.
items.complexity: O(1) time and extra space.

items.title: Append at the tail
items.concept: Without a tail reference, appending requires walking to the last node.
items.prompt: Complete append_node(head, value). Attach one new node at the end and return the head. For None, return the new node.
hints: Handle the empty case first.
Stop when current.next is None, then attach a node.
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space beyond the new node.

items.title: Find a linked value
items.concept: Linked-list search follows references. Random access by index is not available.
items.prompt: Complete linked_find(head, target). Return the zero-based position of the first matching value, or -1.
hints: Count your position while following next.
Return -1 only after reaching the end.
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

items.title: Reverse the links
items.concept: Save the next reference before changing it, or you lose the rest of the chain.
items.prompt: Complete reverse_links(head). Reverse next pointers in place and return the new head. Reuse the original nodes.

tests.label: Case 3
tests.expression: r is b and b.next is a and a.next is None

hints: Remember following = current.next before rewiring.
Move previous and current one step forward.
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

items.title: Find the base case
items.concept: Recursion means a function calls itself. A base case stops further calls.
items.prompt: Complete factorial(n) recursively for integers 0 through 12. Return n!; factorial(0) is 1.
hints: Stop with 1 when n <= 1.
The recursive step is n * factorial(n - 1).
items.complexity: O(n) calls and O(n) call-stack space.

items.title: Sum by recursion
items.concept: An index parameter can shrink a problem without copying a list slice on every call.
items.prompt: Complete recursive_sum(items, index=0). Return the sum from index to the end using recursion. Use indexes; do not slice or call sum().
hints: Stop when index reaches the list length.
Add the current item to the result for index + 1.
items.complexity: O(n) time and call-stack space.

items.title: Climb the Fibonacci steps
items.concept: Naive Fibonacci repeats work. A dictionary can remember results from earlier calls.
items.prompt: Complete fib(n, memo=None) recursively with a memo dictionary. fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1. Inputs are 0 through 30.
hints: Check memo before making more calls.
Store fib(n-1, memo) + fib(n-2, memo).
items.complexity: O(n) time and space with memoization.

items.title: Euclid’s shortcut
items.concept: The greatest common divisor satisfies gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b is zero.
items.prompt: Complete gcd(a, b) recursively for non-negative integers. Return a when b is zero, including gcd(0,0)=0 for this task.
hints: Check b == 0 before computing a remainder.
Pass b and a % b to the next call.
items.complexity: O(log(min(a,b))) recursive steps for positive inputs.

items.starter:
def merge(left, right):
    i = j = 0
    result = []

print(merge([1, 4], [2, 3]))
hints: Continue while both lists still have unused elements.
Append the remainder after one side is exhausted.
items.complexity: O(n + m) time and output space.

items.title: Divide, solve, merge
items.concept: Merge sort divides a list, recursively sorts each half, then merges the sorted halves.
items.prompt: Complete merge_sort(items) recursively. The supplied merge(left, right) helper is ready to use. Return a sorted list without changing the input. Do not use sort() or sorted().
hints: A list of zero or one item is already sorted.
Sort each half before passing them to merge.
items.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) peak auxiliary space.

items.title: Walk a tree in order
items.concept: Inorder traversal visits left subtree, node, then right subtree. A missing child is None.

hints: Return immediately for a None node.
A helper can append into a shared result list.

items.title: Measure tree height
items.concept: For this task, height counts nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path. Empty height is zero.
items.prompt: Complete height(root). An empty tree returns 0; a leaf returns 1. Use recursion.
hints: Find the height of each child.
Choose the larger child height and add one.
items.complexity: O(n) time and O(h) call-stack space.

items.title: Connect the map
items.concept: An adjacency list maps each vertex to its neighbors. Undirected edges go both ways.
items.prompt: Complete adjacency(edges). Input is a list of pairs of distinct string vertices, without duplicate edges. Return a dict of neighbor lists in insertion order. Include vertices appearing in edges.
hints: Create an empty neighbor list when a key is new.
Append b under a and a under b.
items.complexity: O(V + E) time and space.

items.title: Explore one path deeply

hints: Define a visit helper with shared seen and result.
Add the vertex before recursively visiting neighbors.
items.complexity: O(V + E) time and O(V) auxiliary space for reachable vertices.
